subject: Math
subskill: Complete the Square to Standard Form
prompt: In the $xy$-plane, the equation $x^{2}-6x+y^{2}=7$ represents a circle. Which of the following is the standard form of this equation?
explanation: To convert to standard form $(x-h)^{2}+(y-k)^{2}=r^{2}$, complete the square for the $x$ terms. For $x^{2}-6x$, take half of $-6$ to get $-3$, then square it to get $9$. Adding $9$ to both sides: $x^{2}-6x+9+y^{2}=7+9$, which factors as $(x-3)^{2}+y^{2}=16$.
